A_target.statement:
Let $\sequence {X_t}_{t \mathop \ge 0}$ be a [[Definition:Continuous-Time Markov Chain|continuous-time Markov chain]] on a [[Definition:Finite Set|finite]] state space with [[Definition:Transition Rate Matrix|rate matrix]] $Q$.
Then its transition matrices are:
:$\map P t = e^{t Q}$
where $Q$ has non-negative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums.

B_source.statement:
Let $\sequence {X_n}$ be a [[Definition:Markov Chain|discrete-time Markov chain]] with [[Definition:Stochastic Matrix|stochastic]] [[Definition:Transition Matrix|transition matrix]] $P$ and initial distribution $\pi$.
Then the distribution of $X_n$ is:
:$\pi P^n$

substitutions.one discrete step: a time interval of length h

object_map.reformulation: The rate matrix Q must be introduced as the derivative of the transition matrix at time zero, which has no discrete-time counterpart until the step size is made explicit.

validity_conditions: h must be small enough that I + hQ has nonnegative entries, i.e. h <= 1/max|q_ii|
Q must have zero row sums for the approximants to remain stochastic
the state space is taken finite so the matrix exponential converges without further conditions
proof_plan: Fix $t > 0$ and split $\closedint 0 t$ into $n$ steps of size $h = \dfrac t n$.

Approximate the one-step transition matrix over time $h$ by:
:$\map P h \approx \mathbf I + h Q$

For $h$ small, $\mathbf I + h Q$ has non-negative entries, and its rows sum to $1$ as $Q$ has zero row sums.
Hence it is [[Definition:Stochastic Matrix|stochastic]], and the discrete chain is well-defined.

The $n$-step matrix is $\paren {\mathbf I + \dfrac {t Q} n}^n$.
By the [[Definition:Matrix Exponential|matrix exponential]] limit formula:
:$\displaystyle \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \paren {\mathbf I + \frac {t Q} n}^n = e^{t Q}$

From $P^{m + n} = P^m P^n$ in the discrete chain, the limit inherits:
:$\map P {s + t} = \map P s \map P t$
consistent with $e^{\paren {s + t} Q} = e^{s Q} e^{t Q}$.
{{qed}}
